components.css: .ds-route{font-family:'Schibsted Grotesk',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;--c:#f2c230;list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;border-top:1px solid var(--color-rule,#262b33);color:var(--color-paper,#e9ecef);background:var(--color-ink,#0b0d10)}.ds-route a{display:grid;grid-template-columns:2.5rem 1.4fr 1fr;align-items:center;gap:1.5rem;padding:1.6rem 0;border-bottom:1px solid var(--color-rule,#262b33);color:inherit;text-decoration:none;transition:opacity .3s var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1))}.ds-route:hover a:not(:hover){opacity:.35}.ds-stop{position:relative;align-self:stretch;margin:-1.6rem 0}.ds-stop::before{content:'';position:absolute;left:50%;top:-1px;bottom:-1px;width:4px;margin-left:-2px;background:var(--c)}.ds-stop.first::before{top:50%}.ds-stop.last::before{bottom:50%}.ds-stop i{position:absolute;left:50%;top:50%;width:16px;height:16px;margin:-8px 0 0 -8px;box-sizing:border-box;border-radius:50%;background:var(--color-ink,#0b0d10);border:3.5px solid var(--c);transition:transform .3s var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)),background .3s var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1))}.ds-stop i.x{border-color:var(--color-paper,#e9ecef)}.ds-route a:hover .ds-stop i,.ds-route a:focus-visible .ds-stop i{transform:scale(1.35);background:var(--color-paper,#e9ecef)}.ds-t{font-size:1.6rem;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-.025em;line-height:1.1;transition:translate .4s var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1))}.ds-route a:hover .ds-t{translate:.5rem 0}.ds-m{color:var(--color-mute,#9aa1ab);font-size:.95rem}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-route a,.ds-t,.ds-stop i{transition:none}}

components.css: .ds-linerow{font-family:'Schibsted Grotesk',ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif;display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr auto;row-gap:.75rem;padding:0 0 2.25rem;border-bottom:1px solid var(--color-rule,#262b33);color:var(--color-paper,#e9ecef);background:var(--color-ink,#0b0d10);text-decoration:none}.ds-rail{grid-column:1/-1;position:relative;height:2.25rem}.ds-rail::before{content:'';position:absolute;left:0;right:0;top:50%;height:4px;margin-top:-2px;border-radius:2px;background:var(--c);transform-origin:left;transform:scaleX(.18);transition:transform .7s var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1))}.ds-rail i{position:absolute;top:50%;width:11px;height:11px;margin:-5.5px 0 0 -5.5px;box-sizing:border-box;border-radius:50%;background:var(--color-ink,#0b0d10);border:3px solid var(--c);opacity:0;transform:scale(.4);transition:opacity .3s var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)),transform .3s var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1))}.ds-linerow:hover .ds-rail::before,.ds-linerow:focus-visible .ds-rail::before{transform:scaleX(1)}.ds-linerow:hover .ds-rail i,.ds-linerow:focus-visible .ds-rail i{opacity:1;transform:scale(1)}.ds-linerow:hover .ds-rail i:nth-child(2){transition-delay:80ms}.ds-linerow:hover .ds-rail i:nth-child(3){transition-delay:160ms}.ds-name{font-size:2.25rem;font-weight:700;letter-spacing:-.03em;line-height:1.05}.ds-cta{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:.5rem;font-size:.9rem;font-weight:500}.ds-cta svg{transition:transform .3s var(--ease-out, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1))}.ds-linerow:hover .ds-cta svg{transform:translateX(4px)}@media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.ds-rail::before,.ds-rail i{transition:none}}

narrative.overview:
Dakdot is drawn as one transit network. Three service lines (Web, Brand, Motion) carry projects as stations; where a project rides two lines it becomes an interchange, which is where software meets design. The schematic is abstracted, not literal: it appears only where it carries meaning (the hero map, the project index as a route, the line rows, the section terminus and the footer rails). Everything between those moments is quiet: a near-black ground, one grotesk, generous space, hairline rules.

The system is dark-only and flat. Colour belongs to the lines and almost nowhere else; type does the rest of the work at heavy weights with tight tracking. Interaction is the signature: hovering a station or a row lights its route and dims the rest, a cursor-following preview shows the work, and a contextual dot cursor names the action. Motion is damped and short, content is visible by default, and there is one drawing moment per page, not many.

The page refuses the stacked agency template (hero, logo marquee, card grid, bento, FAQ, CTA band). New pages extend the network vocabulary rather than reaching for cards.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ink ground with a three-step tonal ink scale and hairline rules; no light theme.
Three line colours used as strokes, rails and station rings, never as large fills.
One family, Schibsted Grotesk (400 to 900, self-hosted), with tabular numerals on counts.
Strokes run horizontal, vertical or at 45°; stations are hollow rings, interchanges ring in paper.
Pill-shaped actions; 8 to 12px radii for fields, previews and panels.
One ease-out curve for everything; a single route-draw on load; reduced motion honoured throughout.

rules.name: The Lines Own Colour Rule
rules.body: Hue appears only as a line: a stroke, a rail, a ring, a 4px legend swatch. Surfaces stay ink; no tinted panels, no gradients, no coloured section bands.

rules.name: The Text-Safe Tint Rule
rules.body: A line colour used as text, or behind text, switches to its text-safe tint (or, for the red action, to Signal Red). Raw line colours are for strokes.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Schibsted Grotesk is the only face. Hierarchy comes from weight (400 / 500 / 600 / 700 / 800) and tracking, never from a second family.

rules.name: The Heavy-Tight Rule
rules.body: Anything 1.4rem and up is 700 or 800 with negative tracking (-0.025em to -0.04em). Body never goes below 400 or tighter than 0.

rules.name: The Only Floats Cast Rule
rules.body: A shadow means "this is hovering because you pointed at something". Resting surfaces, rows and buttons never carry one.

dos: Do express every service as its line colour, and every project as a station on that line; mark projects on two or more lines as interchanges.
Do switch to the text-safe tint (`web-text`, `brand-text`, `motion-text`) when a line colour must be read, and use Signal Red (`signal-red`) under white text.
Do use the single ease-out curve (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`) for every transition, in the 0.2 to 0.4s range for states and up to 0.7s for rails.
Do keep one drawing moment per page: the map routes draw once on load (1.1s, staggered 140ms), over an always-visible base track, so content is never hidden waiting for animation.
Do honour reduced motion: skip the route draw, smooth scrolling and hover transitions, and snap the cursor to the pointer.
Do keep content inside the 88rem container with the 1.5rem gutter, and split sections asymmetrically rather than centring them.
Do give empty lines capability stops and an honest "See the service" instead of placeholder projects.
donts: Don't fill surfaces or panels with line colour, or use gradients; colour lives in strokes, rails and rings.
Don't draw routes at angles other than 0°, 90° and 45°.
Don't add a second typeface or set headings below 700.
Don't put shadows on resting surfaces; only pointer-driven floats cast them.
Don't rebuild the stacked agency template (hero, logo marquee, card grid, bento, FAQ, CTA band) on new pages; list work as stations on a route.
Don't make the contextual cursor or the cursor-following preview carry information that touch or keyboard users cannot reach.
Don't add a preloader or hide content until an animation runs.
